		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Conventions Used in this Report</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Mobile connected devices</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">We refer to mobile devices, such as traditional mobile phones, smartphones and tablets, that are able to connect to the internet through a cellular, wireless or other network as mobile connected devices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Apps</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">Software applications specifically designed to operate on mobile connected devices are commonly called apps. Mobile connected devices can access information and content either through apps downloaded onto the device or from web</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based mobile sites accessed using a web browser installed on the device. For convenience, unless the context otherwise requires, we refer to these apps and web</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based mobile sites together as apps.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Developers</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">For convenience, we refer to the developers of apps and the publishers of web</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based mobile sites together as developers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Unique users</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss the number of unique users our platform reaches, we measure this as the total number of unique users whose devices made ad requests to our platform during the specified period. This represents the number of users to whom we had an opportunity to deliver ads during that period, not the number of users who actually received ads.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Profiles</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss profiles, we are referring to the number of active unique users in our system that are targetable to receive ads as of the specified date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Audience categories</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss audience categories, we are referring to a grouping of data into a category based on a variety of user attributes, including location, demographics, affluence, intent, gender, and interests.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cross</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#8209;screen users</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss cross</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;screen users, we are referring to users who access digital media through both traditional online means, such as on a laptop or PC, as well as on mobile connected devices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Number of apps</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> and sites</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss the number of apps </font><font style="display: inline;">and sites enabled by </font><font style="display: inline;">developers </font><font style="display: inline;">to </font><font style="display: inline;">receive ads delivered through our platform, we count an app developed for multiple operating systems as multiple apps.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">New and existing clients</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">When we discuss existing clients, we are referring to advertiser clients who had, as of the beginning of the period being discussed, previously advertised on our </font><font style="display: inline;">or </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">platform at any time. An existing client would include a new brand or subsidiary of a parent company that had previously advertised with us</font><font style="display: inline;"> or</font><font style="display: inline;"> Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">. When we discuss new clients, we are referring to advertiser clients who had, as of the beginning of the period being discussed, not previously advertised on either platform.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Business</font><a name="Item1Business_268180"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We are </font><font style="display: inline;">an</font><font style="display: inline;"> independent mobile advertising </font><font style="display: inline;">marketplace</font><font style="display: inline;"> delivering products and services to advertisers and developers. We offer advertisers a suite of solutions that allow them to reach and connect with their target audiences across screens</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">from smartphones, tablets and other mobile </font><font style="display: inline;">devices to PCs&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">with the scale to make significant impact to their business. We offer developers the ability to maximize their advertising revenue and acquire new users for their apps. Our advertiser and developer solutions support all major mobile operating systems, including Apple</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;"> iOS, Android</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2122;</font><font style="display: inline;">, Windows Phone and BlackBerry</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Our </font><font style="display: inline;">propriet</font><font style="display: inline;">ary technology and data</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">platform </font><font style="display: inline;">allows advertisers and developers to interact with us in the way that suits them best. For clients </font><font style="display: inline;">who</font><font style="display: inline;"> want a higher degree of customer service, we </font><font style="display: inline;">offer our &#x201C;managed media&#x201D; services with</font><font style="display: inline;"> dedicated account teams. For our clients </font><font style="display: inline;">who want to interact with us on a more</font><font style="display: inline;"> automated basis, </font><font style="display: inline;">we offer</font><font style="display: inline;"> tools </font><font style="display: inline;">that allow advertisers to buy our ad supply</font><font style="display: inline;"> in a programmatic fashion through our ad exchange</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and developers the opportunity to manage and monetize their ad inventory thro</font><font style="display: inline;">ugh our supply side tool</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The goal of our products and services is to help developers and advertisers remove the complexity from mobile advertising. </font><font style="display: inline;">For developers, we </font><font style="display: inline;">provide tools and services that allow their apps to display video, banner ads, interactive rich media and native ad formats. </font><font style="display: inline;">Through this relationship and access to our platform,</font><font style="display: inline;"> developers gain access to advertising campaigns from brand marketers a</font><font style="display: inline;">nd </font><font style="display: inline;">performance</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based </font><font style="display: inline;">advertisers</font><font style="display: inline;">. In return, developers supply us with space on their apps to deliver ads </font><font style="display: inline;">for our advertiser clients and </font><font style="display: inline;">provide us access to anonymous data associated with their apps and users. We </font><font style="display: inline;">use</font><font style="display: inline;"> data to build </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">sophisticated user profiles</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and audience grou</font><font style="display: inline;">ps that, in combination with our</font><font style="display: inline;"> real</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time decisioning, optimization and targeting capabilities</font><font style="display: inline;">, enable us to deliver</font><font style="display: inline;"> targeted advertising campaigns for our advertiser clients. Advertisers pay us to deliver their </font><font style="display: inline;">campaigns</font><font style="display: inline;"> to mobile users, and we pay developers a fee</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for the use of their ad space. As we deliver more </font><font style="display: inline;">campaigns</font><font style="display: inline;">, we are able to collect additional anonymous data about users, audiences and the effectiveness of particular campaigns, which in turn enhances our targeting capabilities and allows us to deliver better performance for advertisers and better opportunities for developers to increase their revenue streams.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">robust data management platform, or DMP, allows us to access, analyze and utilize the large</font><font style="display: inline;"> volumes of data</font><font style="display: inline;"> we possess. This data includes</font><font style="display: inline;"> location, social, interest, and contextual data, as well as </font><font style="display: inline;">the</font><font style="display: inline;"> insights </font><font style="display: inline;">we derive from measuring campaign</font><font style="display: inline;"> effectiveness</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">provid</font><font style="display: inline;">ing a unique, multidimensional profile</font><font style="display: inline;"> of individual consumer</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">. To date, we have developed more than </font><font style="display: inline;">700</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million active server</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;side unique user profiles, over 60 million of which link multiple mobile devices and PCs to a single specific user on an anonymous basis. These user profiles, combined with third party data </font><font style="display: inline;">from our</font><font style="display: inline;"> data partners, enable</font><font style="display: inline;"> us to deliver more relevant, engaging and effective advertising to our advertising clients. Our data asset also allows us to measure the impact of mobile advertising on consumer engagement, intent and action. We have developed a suite of solutions</font><font style="display: inline;"> which</font><font style="display: inline;"> measure</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> several different areas of mobile advertising impact. As of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, our platform reached more than </font><font style="display: inline;">650</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million monthly</font><font style="display: inline;"> unique users worldwide, including </font><font style="display: inline;">over</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">17</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million</font><font style="display: inline;"> monthly unique users in the United States alone. </font><font style="display: inline;">Approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">60,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> apps and mobile sites are enabled by their developers to receive ads delivered through our platform, and we can deliver ads on over </font><font style="display: inline;">9,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> different mobile device types</font><font style="display: inline;"> and models</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">While averaging more than three billion ad requests daily throughout 2014, i</font><font style="display: inline;">n the last two months of 2014, our platform typically&nbsp;handled over nine billion ad requests daily, including requests received through our supply side tool, and requests received through third party platforms and processed by our programmatic buying tool.</font>
		</p>

Our website address is </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">www.millennialmedia.com.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Information contained in, or accessible through, our website does not constitute a part of, and is not incorporated into, this Annual Report. We completed our initial public offering in March 2012 and our common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">MM</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">. Unless the context requires otherwise, the words </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Millennial Media,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Company,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">we,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">us,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> refer to Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">On December 4, 2014, we completed our acquisition of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage, Inc., or </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage, a privately held mobile advertising exchange and mobile supply side platform under the terms of an Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated September 23, 2014, as amended and restated on October 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of this acquisition, Nexage is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Millennial Media.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with the acquisition of Nexage, we issued an aggregate of </font><font style="display: inline;">30,733,436</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of our common stock to the former securityholders of Nexage and we also issued options to purchase an additional 7,949,236 shares of common stock in exchange for options to purchase shares of Nexage&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the aggregate, the shares issued and </font><font style="display: inline;">shares underlying options represent</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximately 26.4% of the total number of shares of </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> common stoc</font><font style="display: inline;">k following the closing of the merger, </font><font style="display: inline;">assuming the exercise of all new stock options issued in exchange</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the prior Nexage options. </font><font style="display: inline;">Of the </font><font style="display: inline;">total consideration</font><font style="display: inline;">, 4,876,603 of the shares of common stock issued in connection with the acquisition and 1,057,973 of the options exchanged in connection with the acquisition are being held in escrow as partial security for the indemnification </font><font style="display: inline;">obligations of the Nexage securi</font><font style="display: inline;">tyholders</font><font style="display: inline;"> as set forth in the acquisition agreement</font><font style="display: inline;">. We also paid an aggregate of $24.9 million in cash consideration </font><font style="display: inline;">as part of the transaction. All outstanding</font><font style="display: inline;"> warrants exercisable for common stock of Nexage were exchanged for a portion of the 30,733,436 shares of our common stock issued at closing.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Nexage acquisition expands our existing suite of products and </font><font style="display: inline;">comprehensiv</font><font style="display: inline;">e mobile advertising technology with an end-to-end mobile ad exchange and supply side platform that enables advertisers and developers to interact directly with each other in a programmatic, or automated, fashion. We expect to transition our existing ad exchange solution to Nexage&#x2019;s technology and business model in 2015. We believe that the integration of Nexage&#x2019;s supply side platform with our existing supply side tool will improve the solutions we offer to our developers, in particular by increasing access to and optimization of demand sources.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

Each time an app makes</font><font style="display: inline;"> a request to receive an ad,</font><font style="display: inline;"> MYDAS performs several tasks automatically and in real</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time, including identifying unique users; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">targeting ads based on user interest, behavior and location; delivering those ads to millions of users through tens of thousands of apps, running on thousands of different device types; ensuring that the ads will work over wireless connections of varying quality and speed; and measuring user engagement and ad performance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">MYDAS </font><font style="display: inline;">combines proprietary technology with our data in order to deliver the right mobile ad to the right person at the rig</font><font style="display: inline;">ht time in the right place. MYDAS, including the Nexage supply side platform, </font><font style="display: inline;">typically</font><font style="display: inline;"> receives</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">over three billion ad requests daily in the aggregate. MYDAS typically </font><font style="display: inline;">accomplishes </font><font style="display: inline;">ad delivery</font><font style="display: inline;"> in under 50 milliseconds</font><font style="display: inline;"> from ad request</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and includes the following sequences</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Ad request management.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Mobile apps that have our SDKs embedded send a request for an ad to MYDAS through the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">SDK. This ad request enters MYDAS</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, along with associated data from the device, app and mobile carrier. MYDAS analyzes all of the available data to categorize the ad request and to place it in context so that we can deliver the most relevant available ad to the specific user.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Unique user identification.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">MYDAS then runs a proprietary set of algorithms to analyze multiple data points from the device, carrier and app to statistically determine, on an anonymous basis, the likely unique user of the device and the app requesting the ad. In addition, MYDAS can analyze anonymized identifiers sent to us from third parties to identify unique users across devices more accurately. MYDAS assigns an internal unique user identifier to the user profile developed for that individual, with the goal of delivering more relevant ads to that user across multiple mobile devices and maximizing advertising diversity for that user. We believe that many of our competitors rely only upon a device identification code to identify the device as opposed to the more robust analysis that MYDAS employs to identify the unique user. User identification is accomplished on a completely anonymous basis.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Contextual analysis.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">After identifying the unique user associated with a specific advertising request, MYDAS then determines the context around the ad request. This context answers one or more of the following questions:</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:72pt;"><p style="width:72pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Where is the user?</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:72pt;"><p style="width:72pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">What site or app is the user currently using?</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:72pt;"><p style="width:72pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">What is the nature of the content on the site or app from which the request is coming?</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:72pt;"><p style="width:72pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">What type of device is the request coming from?</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:72pt;"><p style="width:72pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">What wireless network is the request coming through?</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Audience analysis.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Once MYDAS identifies the unique user associated with an ad request and its context, it then searches our databases to determine an appropriate audience category or categories based on prior information we have gathered about the user on a completely anonymous basis. For example, a user may belong to an audience of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">moms</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> because she has downloaded or visited several apps focused on content for mothers, or she has identified herself as a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">mom</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in a registration form for an app. We may also place a user in a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">moms</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> audience because she has opted to share location data with us and she has regularly visited retail establishments typically frequented by mothers. We might place another user in an </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;market auto buyer</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> audience because he or she has been in multiple auto dealerships in a short period of time, has opened and engaged with automotive ads and has used numerous apps with automotive</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;focused content. The ability to identify a user and then determine the audiences to which that user belongs is critical in order to deliver the most relevant ad possible to that user and deliver the best results for advertisers and developers. Each time that we see a unique user on our platform, we gain data that enables us to better determine the audiences with which that user should be associated.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">RTB platform.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Real-time bidding, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">RTB</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> is an auction</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;based system in which digital advertising opportunities are auctioned off in real</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;time from developers on an impression</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;by</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;impression basis. Our RTB platform, within MYDAS, was developed to analyze billions of impressions of mobile inventory, in order to deliver effective programmatic buying for advertisers and to increase returns for developers. The RTB platform interacts directly with developers</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> available ad inventory to access scalable audiences in real</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;time. After the bid request is received</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> mmDSP identifies the unique user associated with a specific ad request, the context around the ad request and the audiences to which the user belongs, and delivers the request to our RTB marketplace in which it matches available ads with available ad requests. The real</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;time marketplace can be a virtual auction that we run on behalf of our clients or a real</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;time bidded auction on our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ad </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">exchange or through third party exchanges. mmDSP performs a sophisticated algorithmic analysis to automatically run a near</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;instantaneous auction in which each qualified ad campaign bids on each available ad request. We call this process optimization and decisioning. As part of this decisioning process, we use an artificial intelligence concept called </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">agents,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> which are software programs designed to operate the ad marketplace efficiently and fairly, while at the same time optimizing results based on each campaign</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s goals. Each ad campaign is represented in the marketplace by one of these agents, programmed with specific goals for the particular campaign. The goals will usually include information such as price, audiences to be targeted and timeframe of the campaign, as well as target engagement metrics. When mmDSP enters an ad request into the marketplace, each agent bids on the ad request, and the platform then matches the best available ad to the specific ad request.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">CPC marketplace.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This marketplace is based on display ads and is geared towards performance advertising.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Cross</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#8209;platform ad delivery.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">After matching an ad to a request, MYDAS then delivers, or serves, the ad through the SDK integrated into the app on the specific device making the request. MYDAS can deliver a variety of different types of ads, including video ads, rich media ads, native ad formats and a variety of banner ads, to virtually any mobile connected device across all major mobile operating systems, both within mobile apps and through mobile web browsers. MYDAS can also deliver a variety of ad formats to PCs through online exchanges or through partners with online advertising inventory.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Reporting, analysis and machine learning.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Once MYDAS has delivered an ad to a specific device, MYDAS analyzes the user</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s engagement with the ad, measuring whether the user clicked on the ad or engaged with the ad in some other meaningful way, such as swiping the ad, opening a video, sharing the ad with a friend or downloading an app in response to the ad. These results are </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">then incorporated back into MYDAS</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, which can use the data to analyze whether the specific ad served to the user was actually the best available ad to deliver to that user. This information about the user</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s engagement level with the ad is used to automatically refine various weightings and algorithms within MYDAS to further improve our ability to target and optimize future ad delivery.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">MYDAS </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">also includes a suite of enterprise web services that drive our client</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;facing tools and interfaces like mMedia and our internal workflow tools and interfaces. Our web services layer enables us to build new offerings and scale our platform for developers and advertisers quickly and cost</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;effectively while also enabling us to integrate our solutions with those of third parties.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">MYDAS consists primarily of software incorporating our proprietary algorithms, database software and the data that we store. Our software and data are hosted in data centers in the United States</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. We primarily lease space at data centers on a managed services basis, although we also co</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;locate servers and other equipment that we own at the same data centers. In addition, we use third party web services for some of our data and computing needs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We use techniques that we believe are standard</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in our industry to protect MYDAS</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> against unauthorized access. These techniques include password</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">controlled user access and authentication, secure hosting with firewalls, encryption, load balancers, switches, anti</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;virus software and use of physically secure and redundant facilities.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have increased the average annual spending from this group of advertisers by more than </font><font style="display: inline;">234%</font><font style="display: inline;"> during the period from 2010 to 2014. We</font><font style="display: inline;"> attribute this growth in average spending among these advertisers to our success in capturing advertising campaigns from more brands per advertiser, running more campaigns for each brand per year and supporting larger campaigns from these advertisers. We believe our increased penetration of these 100 advertisers is attributable to increased sales and marketing efforts and our growing reputation for delivering results for large brand advertisers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our largest advertiser and developer clients are typically different from period to period. We believe our business is not substantially dependent on any particular client, and no individual advertising client represented more than 10% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The mobile advertising market is highly competitive. The competitive dynamics of our market are unpredictable because it is in an early stage of development, rapidly evolving, fragmented and subject to potential disruption by new technological innovations. Several competitors provide mobile advertising solutions. Our primary competitors are the large advertising platforms offered by Google and Apple, both of which focus on advertising solutions built for their proprietary mobile operating systems, Android and iOS, respectively. We also compete with in</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;house solutions used by companies who choose to coordinate mobile advertising across their own properties, such </font><font style="display: inline;">as Facebook, Twitter, Yahoo</font><font style="display: inline;">!, and Pandora, as well as some smaller point</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;solution offerings in the mobile advertising market</font><font style="display: inline;">. Some of these companies, such as Facebook and Twitter, have growing mobile advertising networks that coordinate advertising across third party properties as well.</font>
		</p>

We are also continuously working to enhance our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">database of user profiles</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, which enables us to help our advertisers reach and engage more precise audiences developed through demographic and behavioral analysis, and then better measure that improved engagement. As part of our cross</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;platform SDKs that we provide to developers, we seek to include new capabilities, such as additional analytical tools, notification solutions, payment solutions and mediation tools.</font>

We protect our intellectual property through trade secrets law, patents, copyrights, trademarks and contracts. Some of our technology relies upon third party licensed intellectual property.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Government Regulation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We are subject to numerous U.S. and foreign laws and regulations that are applicable to companies engaged in the business of advertising on mobile devices. In addition, many areas of law that apply to our business are still evolving, and could potentially affect our business to the extent they restrict our business practices or impose a greater risk of liability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Given the nascent stage of mobile advertising, industry practices are rapidly evolving. We participate in the Digital Advertising Alliance and other industry groups that are developing best practices for the mobile advertising industry.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Privacy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Privacy and data protection laws play a significant role in our business. In the United States, at both the state and federal level, there are laws that govern activities such as the collection and use of data by companies like us, and privacy and data protection issues generally have gained wide media and public attention recently. Online advertising activities in the United States have primarily been subject to regulation by the Federal Trade Commission, which has regularly relied upon Section&nbsp;5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act to enforce against unfair and deceptive trade practices. Section&nbsp;5 has been the primary regulatory tool used to enforce against alleged violations of online privacy policies, and would apply to privacy practices in the mobile advertising industry. In December 2012, the Federal Trade Commission adopted amendments to rules under the Children</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Online Privacy Protection Act, or COPPA, which went into effect in July 2013. These amendments broaden</font><font style="display: inline;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;"> the potential applicability of COPPA compliance obligations to our activities and those of our clients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The issue of privacy in the mobile advertising industry is still evolving. Federal legislation and rule</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;making has been proposed from time to time that would govern certain advertising practices as they relate to mobile devices, including the use of precise geo</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;location data. Although such legislation has not been enacted, it remains a possibility that such federal and state laws may be passed in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">There have been numerous civil lawsuits, including class action lawsuits, filed against companies that conduct business in the mobile device industry, including makers of mobile devices, mobile application providers, mobile operating system providers, and mobile third party networks. Plaintiffs in these lawsuits have alleged a range of violations of federal, state and common laws, including computer trespass and violation of privacy laws.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition, mobile services are generally not restricted by geographic boundaries, and our services reach mobile devices throughout the world. We currently transact business in Europe and Southeast Asia and, as a result, some of our activities may also be subject to the laws of foreign jurisdictions. In particular, European data protection laws can be more restrictive regarding the collection and use of data than those in U.S. jurisdictions. As we continue to expand into other foreign countries and jurisdictions, we may be subject to additional laws and regulations that may affect how we conduct business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Advertising</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Even though we receive contractual protections from our advertising business partners with respect to their ads, we may nevertheless be subject to regulations concerning the content of ads. Federal and state laws governing intellectual property or other third party rights could apply to the content of ads we place. Laws and regulations regarding unfair and deceptive advertising, sweepstakes, advertising to children, and other consumer protection regulations, may also apply to the ads we place on behalf of clients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Employees</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had </font><font style="display: inline;">636</font><font style="display: inline;"> employees. </font><font style="display: inline;">None of our U.S.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;">based employees are represented by a labor union or covered by a collective bargaining agreement. We consider our relationship with our employees to be good.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Upon consummation of the Merger, all of Nexage&#x2019;s capital stock held by accredited investors and all of its warrants issued and outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Merger were converted into shares of our common stock and cash. In connection with the Merger, we have issued a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">total of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">30,733,436</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> shares</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of our common </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">stock to the former securityholders of Nexage.&nbsp; We have also issued new options to purchase our common stock in exchange for prior options to purchase common stock of Nexage.&nbsp; These newly issued options are, in the aggregate, exercisable for 7,949,236 shares of our common stock. The aggregate potential equity consideration of 38,682,672 shares, including the shares issuable upon the exercise of options, represents approximately 26.4% of the total number of shares of Millennial common stock following the closing of the Merger, but assuming the exercise of all new stock options issued in exchange for the prior Nexage options.&nbsp; Consequently, our stockholders prior to</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the Merger now own a significantly smaller percentage of the combined company and they should expect to exercise less influence over the management and policies of the combined company following the Merger than they previously exercised over our management and policies.</font>

However, there can be no assurance that we will be able to operate Nexage&#x2019;s business profitably or integrate it successfully into our operations in a timely fashion, or at all. The size of the combined company&#x2019;s business is significantly larger than our business was prior to the Merger. Our future success as a combined company depends, in part, upon our ability to manage this expanded business, which will pose substantial challenges for our management, including challenges related to the management and monitoring of new operations and associated increased costs and complexity. The dedication of management resources to this integration could detract attention from our current </font>

Our failure to maintain important customer relationships could harm our reputation, while also negatively impacting our financial condition and results of operations of the combined company.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Risks Related to Our Business and Our Industry</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We have incurred significant net losses since inception, and we expect our operating expenses to increase significantly in the </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">foreseeable future. Accordingly, we may never achieve profitability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We incurred net losses of </font><font style="display: inline;">$149.1</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million and</font><font style="display: inline;"> $15.1</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively, and we had an accumulated deficit of </font><font style="display: inline;">$214.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014. We do not know when or if we will ever achieve profitability. Although our revenue has</font><font style="display: inline;"> increased substantially in recent periods, it is likely that we will not be able to maintain this rate of revenue growth. Historically, our operating expenses have increased in proportion to our revenue. We anticipate that our operating expenses will continue to increase in the foreseeable future to the extent that our revenue grows</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and as we increase headcount</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily driven by the Nexage acquisition.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Additionally, our acquisition</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;related costs may increase if we pursue additional acquisition opportunities. Although we expect to achieve operating efficiencies and greater leverage of resources as we grow, if we are unable to do so, we may be unable to achieve profitability. If we are not able to achieve and maintain profitability, the value of our company and our common stock could decline significantly.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We operate in an intensely competitive industry, and we may not be able to compete successfully.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The mobile advertising market is highly competitive, with numerous companies providing mobile advertising services. We compete primarily with Google and Apple, both of which are significantly larger than us and have more capital to invest in their mobile advertising businesses, and with social networking companies like Facebook and Twitter, that are expanding their own mobile advertising networks.&nbsp; We also compete with in-house solutions used by companies, such as Yahoo! and Pandora, that choose to coordinate mobile advertising across their own properties. They, or other companies that offer competing mobile advertising solutions, may establish or strengthen cooperative relationships with their mobile operator partners, brand advertisers, app developers or other parties, thereby limiting our ability to promote our services and generate revenue. Competitors could also seek to gain market share from us by reducing the prices they charge to advertisers or by introducing new technology tools for developers. Moreover, increased competition for mobile advertising space from developers could result in an increase in the portion of advertiser revenue that we must pay to developers to acquire that advertising space</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our business will suffer to the extent that our developers and advertisers purchase and sell mobile advertising directly from each other or through other companies that are able to become intermediaries between developers and advertisers. For example, we are aware of companies that have substantial existing platforms for developers who had previously not heavily used those platforms for mobile advertising campaigns. These companies could compete with us to the extent they expand into mobile advertising. Other companies, such as large app developers with a substantial mobile advertising business, may decide to directly monetize some or all of their advertising space without utilizing our services. Other companies that offer analytics, mediation, exchange or other third-party services may also become intermediaries between mobile advertisers and developers and thereby compete with us. Any of these developments would make it more difficult for us to sell our services and could result in increased pricing pressure, reduced profit margins, increased sales and marketing expenses or the loss of market share.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">The mobile advertising market may deteriorate or develop more slowly than expected, which could harm our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Advertising on mobile connected devices is an emerging phenomenon. Advertisers have historically spent a smaller portion of their advertising budgets on mobile media as compared to traditional advertising methods, such as television, newspapers, radio and billboards, or online advertising over the internet, such as placing banner ads on websites. Future demand and market acceptance for mobile advertising is uncertain. Many advertisers still have limited experience with mobile advertising and may continue to devote larger portions of their advertising budgets to more traditional offline or online personal computer-based advertising, instead of shifting additional advertising resources to mobile advertising. In addition, our current and potential advertiser clients may ultimately find mobile advertising to be less effective than traditional advertising media or marketing methods or other technologies for promoting their products and services, and they may even reduce their spending on mobile advertising from current levels as a result. If the market for mobile advertising deteriorates, or develops more slowly than we expect, we may not be able to increase our revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our business depends on the continued proliferation of mobile connected devices, such as smartphones and tablets, that can connect to the internet over a cellular, wireless or other network, as well as the increased consumption of content through those devices. Consumer usage of these mobile connected devices may be inhibited for a number of reasons, such as:</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For any of these reasons, users of mobile connected devices may limit the amount of time they spend on these devices and the number of apps they download on these devices. If user adoption of mobile connected devices and consumer consumption of content on those devices do not continue to grow, our total addressable market size may be significantly limited, which could compromise our ability to increase our revenue and to become profitable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">If mobile connected devices, their operating systems or content distribution channels, including those controlled by our primary competitors, develop in ways that prevent our advertising from being delivered to their users, our ability to grow our business will be impaired.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our business model depends upon the continued compatibility of our mobile advertising platform with most mobile connected devices, as well as the major operating systems that run on them and the thousands of apps that are downloaded onto them.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The design of mobile devices and operating systems is controlled by third parties with whom we do not have any formal relationships. These parties frequently introduce new devices, and from time to time they may introduce new operating systems or modify existing ones. Network carriers, such as Verizon, AT&amp;T, Sprint or T-Mobile, may also affect the ability to download apps or access specified content on mobile devices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In some cases, the parties that control the development of mobile connected devices and operating systems include companies that we regard as our most significant competitors. For example, Apple controls two of the most popular mobile devices, the iPhone&#xAE;&nbsp;and the iPad&#xAE;, as well as the iOS operating system that runs on them. Apple also controls the App Store for downloading apps that run on Apple&#xAE;&nbsp;mobile devices. Similarly, Google controls the Android&#x2122; platform operating system. If our mobile advertising platform were unable to work on these devices or operating systems, either because of technological constraints or because a maker of these devices or developer of these operating systems wished to impair our ability to provide ads on them or our ability to fulfill advertising space from developers whose apps are distributed through their controlled channels, our ability to generate revenue could be significantly harmed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">We do not control the mobile networks over which we provide our advertising services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our mobile advertising platform is dependent on the reliability of network operators and carriers who maintain sophisticated and complex mobile networks, as well as our ability to deliver ads on those networks at prices that enable us to realize a profit. Mobile networks have been subject to rapid growth and technological change, particularly in recent years. We do not control these networks.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Mobile networks could fail for a variety of reasons, including new technology incompatibility, the degradation of network performance under the strain of too many mobile consumers using the network, a general failure from natural </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">disaster or a political or regulatory shut-down. Individuals and groups who develop and deploy viruses, worms and other malicious software programs could also attack mobile networks and the devices that run on those networks. Any actual or perceived security threat to mobile devices or any mobile network could lead existing and potential device users to reduce or refrain from mobile usage or reduce or refrain from responding to the services offered by our advertising clients. If the network of a mobile operator should fail for any reason, we would not be able to effectively provide our services to our clients through that mobile network. This in turn could hurt our reputation and cause us to lose significant revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Mobile carriers may also increase restrictions on the amounts or types of data that can be transmitted over their networks. We currently generate different amounts of revenue from our advertiser clients based on the kinds of ads we deliver, such as display ads, rich media ads or video ads. In some cases, we are paid by advertisers on a cost-per-thousand, or CPM, basis depending on the number of ads shown. In other cases, we are paid on a cost-per-click, or CPC, or cost-per-action, or CPA, basis depending on the actions taken by the mobile device user. Different types of ads consume differing amounts of bandwidth and network capacity. If a network carrier were to restrict the amounts of data that can be delivered on that carrier&#x2019;s network, or otherwise control the kinds of content that may be downloaded to a device that operates on the network, it could negatively affect our pricing practices and inhibit our ability to deliver targeted advertising to that carrier&#x2019;s users, both of which could impair our ability to generate revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Mobile connected device users may choose not to allow advertising on their devices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The success of our business model depends on our ability to deliver targeted, highly relevant ads to consumers on their mobile connected devices. Targeted advertising is done primarily through analysis of data, much of which is collected on the basis of user</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;provided permissions. This data might include a device</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s location or data collected when device users view an ad or video or when they click on or otherwise engage with an ad. Users may elect not to allow data sharing for targeted advertising for a number of reasons, such as privacy concerns, or pricing mechanisms that may charge the user based upon the amount or types of data consumed on the device. Users may also elect to opt out of receiving targeted advertising from our platform. In addition, the designers of mobile device operating systems are increasingly promoting features that allow device users to disable some of the functionality, which may impair or disable the delivery of ads on their devices, and device manufacturers may include these features as part of their standard device specifications. Although we are not aware of any such products that are widely used in the market today, as has occurred in the online advertising industry, companies may develop products that enable users to prevent ads from appearing on their mobile device screens. If any of these developments were to occur, our ability to deliver effective advertising campaigns on behalf of our advertiser clients would suffer, which could hurt our ability to generate revenue and become profitable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Our limited operating history makes it difficult to evaluate our business and prospects and may increase your investment risk.</font>

Although we have experienced revenue growth in recent periods, it is likely that we will not be able to sustain this growth. As part of the nascent mobile advertising industry, we will encounter risks and difficulties frequently encountered by early</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;stage companies in rapidly evolving industries, including the need to:</font>
