			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Revenue was </font><font style="display: inline;">$296.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million for the year ended December 31, 2014 compared to </font><font style="display: inline;">$259.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of </font><font style="display: inline;">$37.0</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">14.3%</font><font style="display: inline;">. Revenue</font><font style="display: inline;"> for </font><font style="display: inline;">2014 includes revenue from Nexage of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the period from December 5, 2014 to December 31, 2014. The remaining growth was primarily attributable </font><font style="display: inline;">to a full year of Jumptap revenue and the related</font><font style="display: inline;"> increase in spending from our existing advertiser clients</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as an increase in the number of advertiser clients using our platform</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Jumptap acquisition was completed on November 6, 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;">Revenue from our existing advertiser clients increased by </font><font style="display: inline;">16.6%</font><font style="display: inline;"> during the year ended December 31, 2014 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and represented </font><font style="display: inline;">89.3%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of our total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2014. The increase in revenue from existing clients was driven both by our acquisitions and by additional campaigns from brand and performance advertisers that had previously advertised with us, larger campaign sizes and campaigns for new brands owned by existing clients. Revenue from new advertiser clients decreased by </font><font style="display: inline;">3.1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> during the year ended December 31, 2014 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and represented </font><font style="display: inline;">10.7%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of our total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2014.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our revenue from international operations was </font><font style="display: inline;">$48.1</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">16.2%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of total revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2014 compared to </font><font style="display: inline;">$62.1</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">24.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of total revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease in revenue in our international operations was primarily driven by certain large, international performance clients, who spent significan</font><font style="display: inline;">tly less with us in 2014 versus</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2013.</font>

Therefore, we may sell a campaign to a large performance advertiser in one location, such as Europe, and principally deliver ads for that campaign to consumers located in the United States. </font>

The increase in cost of revenue in absolute dollars was the direct result of the increase in revenue, as we pay a percentage of that revenue to developers for use of their ad space in delivering mobile ads for our advertising clients.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Sales and marketing.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Sales and marketing expense was </font><font style="display: inline;">$53.6</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">18.1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2014, an increase of </font><font style="display: inline;">$14.9</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">38.6%</font><font style="display: inline;">, from </font><font style="display: inline;">$38.7</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">14.9%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase in sales and marketing expense, both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue, was primarily attributable to a </font><font style="display: inline;">$7.9</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million increase in salaries and personnel</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;related costs associated with an increase in headcount, as we increased the number of sales and marketing personnel to support and expand our client base.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also experienced higher commission costs associated with higher revenue. The number of full</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time sales and marketing employees was </font><font style="display: inline;">224</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December 31, 2014, which is an increase from </font><font style="display: inline;">187</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December&nbsp;31, 2013. As a result of the Nexage acquisition we added </font><font style="display: inline;">17</font><font style="display: inline;"> sales and marketing employees. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from December 5, 2014 to December 31, 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">As a result of the Jumpt</font><font style="display: inline;">ap acquisition we added 40 sales and marketing employees in November 2013. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from November 6, 2013 to December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> for 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;">2014 includes the</font><font style="display: inline;"> full year impact of these Jumpt</font><font style="display: inline;">ap employees. In addition, we experienced an additional</font><font style="display: inline;"> $4.1 million in depreciation and amortization,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$1.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in travel and travel related expenses and an </font><font style="display: inline;">$812,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> increase in our marketing programs and travel expenses. </font>

The increase in technology and development expense, in absolute dollars</font><font style="display: inline;"> and as a percentage of revenue</font><font style="display: inline;">, was primarily attributable to a </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.6</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million increase in salaries and personnel</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;related costs associated with an increase in the full year headcount, partially offset by a decrease in stock compensation expense of </font><font style="display: inline;">$958,000</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;primarily associated with a one</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time cost recorded in the prior year related to the departure of certain employees in the technology and development functions and acceleration of unvested stock awards. As a result of the Jumpt</font><font style="display: inline;">ap acquisition we added 51 technology and development employees in November 2013. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from November 6, 2013 to December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> for 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">. 2014 includes the</font><font style="display: inline;"> full year impact of these Jumpt</font><font style="display: inline;">ap employees. The number of full</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time general and administrative employees was </font><font style="display: inline;">258</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December 31, 2014, a decrease from </font><font style="display: inline;">270</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December&nbsp;31, 2013. 		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Revenue was $259.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to $177.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, an increase of $81.5&nbsp;million, or 45.9%. 2013 revenue includes revenue from Jumptap of $25.6 million for the period from November&nbsp;6, 2013 to December&nbsp;31, 2013. This growth was primarily attributable to an increase in spending from our existing advertiser clients as well as an increase in the number of advertiser clients using our platform. Revenue from our existing advertiser clients increased by 52.8% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and represented 87.3% of our total revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase in revenue from existing clients was driven by additional campaigns from brand and performance advertisers that had previously advertised with us, larger campaign sizes and campaigns for new brands owned by existing clients. Revenue from new advertiser clients increased by 8.9% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and represented 12.7% of our total revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our revenue from international operations was $62.1&nbsp;million, or 24.0% of total revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to $26.2&nbsp;million, or 14.8% of total revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. This revenue growth in our international operations was primarily driven by certain large, international performance clients, though revenue increased across a number of clients globally in 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We classify revenue based on the geographic location where the advertising was sold. Performance advertising often is displayed globally. Therefore, we may sell a campaign to a large performance advertiser in one location, such as Europe, and principally deliver ads for that campaign to consumers located in the United States. As a result, our revenue from advertising delivered to U.S. consumers was higher than the revenue derived from advertising sold in the United States in 2013.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We also substantially increased our overall sales force during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to the prior year, allowing us to increase our number of advertising client relationships and the number of developer applications enabled to receive ads delivered through our platform.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Cost of revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cost of revenue was $154.8&nbsp;million, or 59.7% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of $49.1&nbsp;million, or 46.4%, from $105.7&nbsp;million, or 59.5% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in cost of revenue in absolute dollars was the direct result of the increase in revenue, as we pay a percentage of that revenue to developers for use of their ad space in delivering mobile ads for our advertising clients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Sales and marketing.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales and marketing expense was $38.7&nbsp;million, or 14.9% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of $14.9&nbsp;million, or 62.4%, from $23.8&nbsp;million, or 13.4% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in sales and marketing expense, both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue, was primarily attributable to a $9.8&nbsp;million increase in salaries and personnel-related costs associated with an increase in headcount and stock-based compensation expense, as we increased the number of sales and marketing personnel to support our expanding client base and experienced higher commission costs associated with higher revenue. The number of full-time sales and marketing employees was 187 at December&nbsp;31, 2013, which is an increase from 113 at December&nbsp;31, 2012. As a result of the Jumptap acquisition we added 40 sales and marketing employees. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from November&nbsp;6, 2013 to December&nbsp;31, 2013. In addition, we experienced a $2.5&nbsp;million increase in our marketing programs and travel expenses, an additional $509,000 in depreciation expense related to our property and equipment, an additional $531,000 in amortization expense for acquired intangible assets, an additional $723,000 in rent expense, $801,000 in severance payments which resulted from the acquisition of Jumptap, and an additional $100,000 in other general sales and marketing costs to support our growing sales force.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Technology and development.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Technology and development expense was $19.0&nbsp;million, or 7.3% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of $5.4&nbsp;million, or 39.3%, from $13.6&nbsp;million, or 7.7% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in technology and development expense, in absolute dollars, was primarily attributable to a $5.2&nbsp;million increase in salaries and personnel-related costs associated with an increase in headcount, partially offset by a decrease in stock compensation expense of $2.1&nbsp;million primarily associated with a one-time cost recorded in the prior year related to the departure of certain employees in the technology and development functions and acceleration of unvested stock awards. The number of full-time technology and development employees was 143 at December&nbsp;31, 2013, which is an increase from 79 at December&nbsp;31, 2012. As a result of the Jumptap acquisition we added 51 technology and development employees. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from November&nbsp;6, 2013 to December&nbsp;31, 2013. In addition, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we incurred $780,000 in increased depreciation expense related to our property, equipment, and internally developed software, an additional $765,000 in amortization expense for acquired intangible assets, an additional $107,000 in rent expense, an additional $162,000 in travel related activities, an additional $334,000 in production server hosting expenses, and $95,000 in severance payments as a result of the acquisition of Jumptap. The decrease in technology and development expenses as a percentage of revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 was primarily attributable to our revenue growing faster than our expenses during 2013, but was also affected by the $2.1&nbsp;million of higher stock-based compensation expense for our technology and development employees in the prior year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">General and administrative.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;General and administrative expense was $61.9&nbsp;million, or 23.9% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of $22.9&nbsp;million, or 58.9%, from $39.0&nbsp;million, or 21.9% of revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in general and administrative expense was primarily attributable to a $9.4&nbsp;million increase in salaries and personnel-related costs associated with an increase in headcount and stock compensation expense. In addition, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we incurred $7.6&nbsp;million of acquisition-related costs and severance related to the Jumptap and Metaresolver acquisitions, increased professional service fees of $1.3&nbsp;million, $1.0&nbsp;million in increased depreciation and amortization expense related to our property, equipment, and internally developed software, $750,000 of deferred compensation expense related to our acquisition of Metaresolver, increased rent expense of $475,000, increased information system costs of $272,000, and an increase of $2.1&nbsp;million in other general corporate costs necessary to support the overall growth in our business. The number of full-time general and administrative employees was 270 at December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase from 156 at December&nbsp;31, 2012. As a result of the Jumptap acquisition we added 64 general and administrative employees. These employees and corresponding expenses only affected the period from November&nbsp;6, 2013 to December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">53</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Income tax benefit.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we recognized an income tax benefit of $47,000 primarily due to investment tax credits in Singapore, partially offset by minimal state and foreign tax liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Seasonality</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our revenue tends to be seasonal in nature, with the fourth quarter of each calendar year historically representing the largest percentage of our total revenue for the year, and the first quarter representing our smallest percentage of total revenue for the year. Many brand advertisers spend the largest portion of their advertising budgets during the fourth quarter, in preparation for the holiday season.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Inflation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We do not believe that inflation has had a material effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. We continue to monitor the impact of inflation in order to minimize its effects through pricing strategies, productivity improvements and cost reductions. If our costs were to become subject to significant inflationary pressures, we may not be able to fully offset such higher costs through price increases. Our inability or failure to do so could harm our business, financial condition and results of operations</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Sources of Liquidity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2014, we had cash and cash equivalents totaling </font><font style="display: inline;">$49.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. In August 2011, we entered into a line of credit with Silicon Valley Bank, or SVB, which allowed for borrowings up to </font><font style="display: inline;">$15.0</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million. Amounts borrowed under the line of credit are secured by all of our assets. </font><font style="display: inline;">The loan agreement was amended in October 2013 to extend the maturity date to May 9, 2014, to revise the interest rate payable under the agreement and to make other changes. The loan agreement was amended again in May 2014 increasing allowed borrowings under the agreement to $20.0 million. </font><font style="display: inline;">The loan agreement was amended </font><font style="display: inline;">and restated </font><font style="display: inline;">in November 2014, increasing allowed borrowings to $40.0 million</font><font style="display: inline;"> and making other changes</font><font style="display: inline;">. Advances under the line of credit bear interest at a floating rate equal to, at </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> option, either the prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal plus a margin of 1.6% or the ICE Benchmark Administration LIBOR rate plus a margin of 2.6%, </font><font style="display: inline;">in either case </font><font style="display: inline;">with interest payable monthly. The line of credit agreement requires that </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;"> maintain a ratio of cash, cash equivalents and billed accounts receivable to current liabilities less the current portion of deferred revenue of at least 1.25 to 1.00. There are also EBITDA minimum requirements under the credit agreement. Additionally, the line of credit agreement contains an unused line fee of 0.2% per year, calculated based on the average unused portion of the loan, payable monthly. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2014, we had not yet drawn on this line of credit. As of December 31, 2014, we were in compliance with all covenants under the loan agreement. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reported period. In accordance with U.S. GAAP, we base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that we believe are reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results may differ from these estimates.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We recognize revenue based on the activity of mobile users viewing ads through developer applications and mobile websites. Our revenue is recognized when our advertising services are delivered based on the specific terms of the advertising contract, which are commonly based on the number of ads delivered, or views, clicks or actions by users on mobi</font><font style="display: inline;">le advertisements. At the time that</font><font style="display: inline;"> our services have been provided, the fees charged are fixed or determinable, persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, and collectability is reasonably assured.</font>
		</p>

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">establishing prices, are responsible for fulfillment of the transaction, have credit risk, or have several but not all of these indicators, </font><font style="display: inline;">we recognize </font><font style="display: inline;">revenue on a gross basis. While none of the factors individually are considered presumptive or determinative, in reaching our conclusions on gross versus net revenue recognition, we place the most weight on the analysis of whether or not we are the primary obligor in the arrangement. We generally record t</font><font style="display: inline;">he net amounts as revenue </font><font style="display: inline;">earned if we are not primarily obligated or do not have latitude in establishing prices or credit risk. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We record deferred revenue when we receive cash payments from our advertiser clients in advance of when we perform the services under our arrangements with them.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable and Allowances for Doubtful Accounts and Sales Credits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Accounts receivable are stated at realizable value, net of an allowance for doubtful accounts that we maintain for estimated losses expected to result from the inability of some clients to make payments as they become due. Our estimated allowance is based on our analysis of past due amounts and ongoing credit evaluations. Historically, our actual collection experience has not varied significantly from our estimates, due primarily to our credit and collection policies and the financial strength of many of our clients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We also estimate an allowance for sales credits based on our historical experience of sales credits as a percentage of revenue. Historically, actual sales credits have not significantly differed from our estimates. However, if our revenue and client base continues to grow, higher than expected sales credits may result in future write</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;offs that are greater than our estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Business Combinations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In business combinations, we determine the acquisition purchase price as the sum of the consideration we provide. When we issue stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based awards to an acquired company&#x2019;s selling stockholders or employees, we evaluate whether the awards are purchase consideration or compensation for post</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;business combination services. Our evaluation includes, among other things, whether the vesting of the stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based awards is contingent on the continued employment of the selling stockholder beyond the acquisition date. If continued employment is required for vesting, the awards are treated as compensation for post</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;acquisition services and recognized as future compensation expense over the required service period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We allocate the purchase price in a business combination to the identifiable assets and liabilities of the acquired business at their acquisition date fair values. The excess of the purchase price over the amount allocated to the identifiable assets and liabilities, if any, is recorded as goodwill.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">To date, the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in our business combinations have primarily consisted of acquired working capital and definite</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived intangible assets. Working capital is recorded at its fair value. We estimate the fair value of definite</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived intangible assets acquired using a discounted cash flow approach, which includes an analysis of the future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset and the risk associated with achieving these cash flows. The key assumptions used in the discounted cash flow model include the discount rate that is applied to the forecasted future cash flows to calculate the present value of those cash flows and the estimate of future cash flows attributable to the acquired intangible asset, which include revenue, operating expenses and taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stock</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#8209;Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We include stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation as part of operating expenses in connection with the grant or modification of stock options and other equity awards to our directors, employees and non</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;employees. We apply the fair value method in accordance with authoritative guidance for determining the cost of stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation. The total cost of the grant is measured based on the estimated fair value of the award at the date of grant. Modifications are measured based on the fair value at the date of modification. The fair value is then recognized as stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation expense over the requisite service period, which is the vesting period, of the award. Information about the assumptions used in the calculation of stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation expense is set forth in the Stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;Based Compensation footnote to our consolidated financial statements included under Item&nbsp;8 of this Annual Report.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display: inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Intangible Asset Impairment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We review long-lived assets and certain identifiable intangible assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability of the long-lived asset is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of the asset or asset group to future undiscounted net cash flows expected to be generated by the asset or asset group. If such assets are not recoverable, the impairment to be recognized, if any, is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the estimated fair value of the assets or asset group.&nbsp;&nbsp;As we operate as one business unit and our long-lived assets do not have identifiable cash flows that are independent of the other assets and liabilities of this business unit, the intangible asset test is performed at the entity level.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During the year ended December 31, 2014, we determined that our technology and customer relationship assets were not fully recoverable due to lower projected revenue levels from associated products and customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, we recognized an impairment charge of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$36.4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million to reduce the carrying values of these intangible assets to their estimated fair values.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value was estimated using the income approach based on management&#x2019;s forecast of future cash flows to be derived from the asset&#x2019;s use.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> We continue to evaluate the fair value of our intangible assets based on the results of our operations. Depending on our operations, we may in the future be required to record additional impairment charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Goodwill Impairment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Goodwill is tested annually for impairment on October 1 of each year or more frequently if impairment indicators arise.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level using a two</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:MS Mincho;color:#000000;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">step approach. The first step is to compare the fair value of the reporting unit to the carrying value of the net assets assigned to the reporting unit. If the fair value of the reporting unit is greater than the carrying value of the net assets assigned to the reporting unit, the assigned goodwill is not considered impaired. If the fair value is less than the reporting unit&#x2019;s carrying value, step two is performed to measure the amount of the impairment, if any.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During the year ended December 31, 2014, we determined sufficient indication existed to require performance of an interim goodwill impairment analysis as of September 30, 2014 for our reporting unit.&nbsp;&nbsp;This indicator was a decrease in our market capitalization below the carrying value of our net assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;In this interim goodwill impairment test, the reporting unit failed step one.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The combination of the lower reporting unit fair value calculated in step one and the identification of unrecognized fair value changes to the carrying values of other assets and liabilities in the second step of the interim goodwill impairment test, resulted in an implied fair value of goodwill below the carrying value of goodwill.&nbsp; As a result, we r</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ecorded a</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> goodwill impairment loss </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$57.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million. We continue to evaluate the fair value of our goodwill based on the results of our operations. Depending on our operations, we may in the future be required to record additional impairment charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the </font><font style="display: inline;">Financial Accounting Standards Board, or </font><font style="display: inline;">FASB</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Update, or </font><font style="display: inline;">ASU</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> No. 2014-09, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU No. 2014-09 supersedes the revenue recognition requirements in </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Codification, or ASC, </font><font style="display: inline;">Topic 605, Revenue Recognition. The adoption of ASU No. 2014-09 is required for public entities for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is evaluating what the effects, if any, of the adoption of ASU No. 2014-09 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font><a name="Item7AQuantitativeandQualitativeDisclosu"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Market risk is the risk of loss to future earnings, to fair values or to future cash flows that may result from changes in the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in interest rates, exchange rates, commodity prices, equity prices and other market changes. We are exposed to market risk related to changes in foreign currency exchange rates. We do not use derivative financial instruments for speculative, hedging or trading purposes, although in the future we may enter into exchange rate hedging arrangements to manage the risks described below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Rate Sensitivity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We maintain a short</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;term investment portfolio consisting mainly of highly liquid short</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;term money market funds, which we consider to be cash equivalents. These investments earn interest at variable rates and, as a result, decreases in market interest rates would generally result in decreased interest income. Any borrowings under our line of credit with SVB are at a variable rate and, as a result, increases in market interest rates would generally result in increased interest expense on our outstanding borrowings. During 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, we did not have any borrowings outstanding under the line of credit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Foreign Currency Exchange Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">With international operations, we face exposure to adverse movements in foreign currency exchange rates. These exposures may change over time as business practices evolve and if our exposure increases, adverse movement in foreign currency exchange rates would have a material adverse impact on our financial results. Historically, our primary exposures have been related to non</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;U.S. dollar denominated operating expenses in the United Kingdom, other countries in Europe, and Singapore. As a result, our results of operations would generally be adversely affected by a decline in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to these foreign currencies. However, based on the size of our international operations and the amount of our expenses denominated in foreign currencies, we would not expect a 10% decline in the value of the U.S. dollar from rates on </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> to have a material effect on our financial position or results of operations. Substantially all of our sales contracts are currently denominated in U.S. dollars. Therefore, we have minimal foreign currency exchange risk with respect to our revenue.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font><a name="REPORTOFINDEPENDENTREGISTEREDPUBLICACCOU"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders of Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc.:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have audited Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, based on criteria established in Internal Control</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (</font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> framework) (the COSO criteria). Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in Management</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appearing in Item&nbsp;9A. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As indicated in Management</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appearing in Item&nbsp;9A, management</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s assessment of and conclusion on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting did not include the internal controls of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">,&nbsp;Inc</font><font style="display: inline;">., which is included in the 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> consolidated financial statements of Millennial</font><font style="display: inline;"> Media,&nbsp;Inc. and consti</font><font style="display: inline;">tuted $20.8&nbsp;million and $1.5</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million of total and net assets, respectively, as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $1.4</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million and</font><font style="display: inline;"> $703</font><font style="display: inline;">,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenues and net loss, respectively, for the year then ended. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting of Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. also did not include an evaluation of the internal control over financial reporting of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">,&nbsp;Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In our opinion, Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, based on the COSO criteria.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheets of Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, stockholders</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">equity </font><font style="display: inline;">(deficit), and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Millennial Media,&nbsp;In</font><font style="display: inline;">c., and our report dated March&nbsp;11</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> an</font><font style="display: inline;">d 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, changes in stockholders</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">equity (deficit)</font><font style="display: inline;">, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">. These financial statements and schedule are the responsibility of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements and schedule based on our audits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

Also, in our opinion, the related financial statement schedule, when considered in relation to the basic financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly in all material respects the information set forth therein.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, based on criteria established in Internal Control</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations </font><font style="display: inline;">of the Treadway Commission (2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> framework) an</font><font style="display: inline;">d our report dated March&nbsp;11</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:times;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">1. Description of Business</font><a name="a1DescriptionofBusiness_811528"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) was incorporated in the state of Delaware in May 2006. The Company is engaged in the business of providing mobile advertising solutions to advertisers and developers. Its technology, tools and services help developers to maximize their advertising revenue, acquire users and gain insight about their users. The Company offers advertisers significant audience reach, sophisticated targeting capabilities and the ability to deliver rich and engaging ad experiences to consumers on their mobile connected devices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">2. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Principles of Consolidation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Millennial Media,&nbsp;Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries. All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In July 2013, the </font><font style="display: inline;">Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">FASB</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;) issued </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) No. 2013-11, &#x201C;Income Taxes (Topic 740)&#x201D;. ASU No. 2013-11 requires that an unrecognized tax benefit, or a portion of an unrecognized tax benefit, be presented in the financial statements as a reduction to a deferred tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward, with certain exceptions. This guidance is effective for annual and interim reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2013. The adoption of ASU </font><font style="display: inline;">No. 2013-11 </font><font style="display: inline;">did not have a material impact on the Company's consolidated financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU No. 2014-09, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU No. 2014-09 supersedes the revenue recognition requirements in </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;">Topic 605, Revenue Recognition. The adoption of ASU No. 2014-09 is required for public entities for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is evaluating what the effects, if any, of the adoption of ASU No. 2014-09 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Use of Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles (&#x201C;U.S.&nbsp;GAAP&#x201D;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On an ongoing basis, the Company evaluates its estimates, including those related to the accounts receivable allowances, the useful lives of long</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived assets and other intangible assets, assumptions used for purposes of determining stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation, identification of intangibles in purchase accounting, </font><font style="display: inline;">contingent liabilities, fair value of intangibles and goodwill </font><font style="display: inline;">and income taxes, among others. The Company bases its estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that it believes to be reasonable, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying value of assets and liabilities as well as reporting revenue and expenses during the periods presented.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents consist of checking accounts and a money market account. The Company considers all highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase to be cash equivalents. The Company maintains cash balances in financial institutions in amounts greater than federally insured limits.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition and Deferred Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> recognize</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> revenue based on the activity of mobile users viewing ads through developer applica</font><font style="display: inline;">tions and mobile websites. R</font><font style="display: inline;">evenue</font><font style="display: inline;">s are recognized when </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> advertising services are delivered based on the specific terms of the advertising contract, which are commonly based on the number of ads delivered, or views, clicks or actions by users on mobile a</font><font style="display: inline;">dvertisements. At </font><font style="display: inline;">such time,</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> services have been provided, the fees charged are fixed or determinable, persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, and collectability is reasonably assured.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> evaluate</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> whether it is appropriate to recognize revenue based on the gross amount billed to the customers or the ne</font><font style="display: inline;">t amount earned as revenue</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">W</font><font style="display: inline;">hen the Company is</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily </font><font style="display: inline;">obligated in a transaction, has</font><font style="display: inline;"> lati</font><font style="display: inline;">tude in establishing prices, is</font><font style="display: inline;"> responsible for fulf</font><font style="display: inline;">illment of the transaction, has credit risk, or has</font><font style="display: inline;"> several but not all of these indicators, revenue is recorded on a gross basis. While none of the factors individually are considered presumptive o</font><font style="display: inline;">r determinative, in reaching</font><font style="display: inline;"> conclusions on gross ve</font><font style="display: inline;">rsus net revenue recognition, the Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> place</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> the most weight on t</font><font style="display: inline;">he analysis of whether or not it is</font><font style="display: inline;"> the primary obligor in the arran</font><font style="display: inline;">gement. The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> reco</font><font style="display: inline;">rd</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> the net amounts as revenue </font><font style="display: inline;">earned if it is</font><font style="display: inline;"> not primarily obligated or do</font><font style="display: inline;">es</font><font style="display: inline;"> not have latitude in esta</font><font style="display: inline;">blishing prices or credit risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred revenue arises as a result of differences between the timing of revenue recognition and receipt of cash from the Company&#x2019;s customers. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cost of Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cost of revenue consists primarily of amounts due to developers for the advertising inventory utilized in running mobile advertisements. These amounts are typically either a percentage of the advertising revenue earned by the Company based on mobile advertisements that are run on each developer&#x2019;s application or a fixed fee for the ad space or fees paid to win bids for advertising inventory purchased from auction</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based marketplace exchanges. The Company recognizes the cost of revenue as the associated revenue is recognized, on a developer by developer basis during the period the advertisements run on the developer&#x2019;s advertising application or mobile website. Costs owed to developers but not yet paid are recorded as accrued cost of revenue. The cost of revenue for ads delivered through auction</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based exchanges can vary depending on the Company&#x2019;s ability to purchase inventory at competitive rates to win the auction bid.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurements</font>

The hierarchy requires the Company to use observable inputs when available, and to minimize the use of unobservable inputs when determining fair value. The three tiers are defined as follows:</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Money market funds are classified as cash equivalents in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated balance sheets. As short</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#8209;term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known amounts of cash, with remaining maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase, the Company&#x2019;s cash equivalent money market funds have carrying values that approximate fair value. Amounts do not include </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$24.5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;million and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$30.8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;million of operating cash balances as of De</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">cember 31, 2014 and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> 2013, respectively.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Assets and Liabilities M</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">easured at Fair Value on a Nonr</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">ecurring Basis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Some assets are not measured at fair value on an ongoing basis but are subject to fair value adjustments only in certain circumstances. These assets can include </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">goodwill and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">intangible assets </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">(customer relationships, technology and intellectual property</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">that have been reduced to fair value when they are impaired (see Note 5). Assets that are written down to fair value when impaired are not subsequently adjusted to fair value unless further impairment occurs.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">These assets and liabilities also include those related to business acquisitions that are recorded at fair value upon acquisition (see Note 3).</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">These nonrecurring fair value measurements are based on significant inputs not observable in the market and represent Level 3 measurements within the fair value hierarchy.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company uses a combination of income-based and market-based approaches to estimate the fair value of goodwill. These approaches use significant unobservable inputs, including forecasted revenues, gross profit margins, working capital requirements, perpetual growth rates and long-term discount rates.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The Company used an income-based approach, specifically the multi-period excess earnings approach to estimate the fair value of our customer relationship asset. This approach used significant unobservable inputs, including forecasted revenues and expense, a long-term discount rate and an estimate for the retention/churn rate of our customers. The Company also used an income-based approach, specifically the relief from royalty method to estimate the fair value of our technology asset. This approach used significant unobservable inputs including projected revenues and market observations regarding royalty rates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Concentration of Credit Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Financial instruments that subject the Company to significant concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents and accounts receivable. All of the Company&#x2019;s cash and cash equivalents are held at financial institutions that the Company believes to be of high credit quality. The Company&#x2019;s cash and cash equivalent accounts exceed federally insured limits at times. The Company has not experienced any losses on cash and cash equivalents to date. To manage accounts receivable risk, the Company evaluates the creditworthiness of its customers and maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2014 </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for more than </font><font style="display: inline;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenue and </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for greater than 10% of outstanding receivables at year end. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for more than </font><font style="display: inline;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenue and </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for greater than </font><font style="display: inline;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of outstanding receivables at year end.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts and Sales Credits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company extends credit to customers without requiring collateral. Accounts receivable are stated at realizable value, net of an allowance for doubtful accounts. The Company utilizes the allowance method to provide for doubtful accounts based on the Company&#x2019;s evaluation of the collectability of amounts due. The Company&#x2019;s estimate is based on historical collection experience and a review of the current status of accounts receivable. Historically, actual write</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;offs for uncollectible accounts have not significantly differed from the Company&#x2019;s estimates. However, higher than expected bad debts may result in future write</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;offs that are greater than the Company&#x2019;s estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company also estimates an allowance for sales credits based on the Company&#x2019;s historical sales credits experience. Historically, actual sales credits have not significantly differed from the Company&#x2019;s estimates. However, higher than expected sales credits may result in future write</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;offs that are greater than the Company&#x2019;s estimates. The allowances for doubtful accounts and sales credits are included in accounts receivable, net in the consolidated balance sheets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Property and Equipment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Property and equipment are recorded at cost. Expenditures for major additions and improvements are capitalized. Depreciation and amortization is provided over the estimated useful lives of the related assets using the straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line method.</font>
		</p>
