			<font style="display: inline;">Repairs and maintenance costs are charged to expense as incurred.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Internally Developed Software</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company capitalizes certain internal and external software development costs, consisting primarily of direct labor associated with creating the internally developed software. Software development projects generally include </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> stages: the preliminary project stage (all costs expensed as incurred), the application development stage (costs are capitalized) and the post</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;">implementation/</font><font style="display: inline;">operation stage (all costs expensed as incurred). The costs capitalized in the application development stage primarily include the costs of designing the application, coding and testing of the system. Capitalized costs are amortized using the straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line method over the estimated useful life of the software</font><font style="display: inline;">, generally 3 years,</font><font style="display: inline;"> once it is ready for its intended use. The Company believes the straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line recognition method best approximates the manner in which the expected benefit will be derived. Capitalized software development costs of </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.9</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.5</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million have been included in property and equipment in the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively. Amortization expense for the related capitalized internally developed software for the years ended December 31, 2014, 2013, and 2012 totaled </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and </font><font style="display: inline;">$723,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively, and is included in technology and development and general and administrative expenses in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Business Combinations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In business combinations, the Company determines the acquisition purchase price as the sum of the consideration provided. When stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based awards are issued to an acquired company&#x2019;s selling stockholders or employees, the Company evaluates whether the awards are purchase consideration or compensation for post</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;business combination services. This evaluation includes, among other things, whether the vesting of the stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based awards is contingent on the continued employment of the selling stockholder beyond the acquisition date. If continued employment is required for vesting, the awards are treated as compensation for post</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;acquisition services and recognized as future compensation expense over the required service period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company allocates the purchase price in a business combination to the identifiable assets and liabilities of the acquired business at their acquisition date fair values. The excess of the purchase price over the amount allocated to the identifiable assets and liabilities, if any, is recorded as goodwill.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">To date, the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in business combinations have primarily consisted of acquired working capital and definite</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived intangible assets. Working capital is recorded at its fair value. The Company estimates the fair value of definite</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived intangible assets acquired using a discounted cash flow approach, which includes an analysis of the future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset and the risk associated with achieving these cash flows. The key assumptions used in the discounted cash flow model include the discount rate that is applied to the forecasted future cash flows to calculate the present value of those cash flows and the estimate of future cash flows attributable to the acquired intangible asset, which include revenue, operating expenses and taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Goodwill</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill represents the excess of: (a)&nbsp;the aggregate of the fair value of consideration transferred in a business combination, over (b)&nbsp;the fair value of assets acquired, net of liabilities assumed. Goodwill is not amortized, but is subject to an annual impairment test. The Company tests goodwill for impairment annually on October&nbsp;1st&nbsp;or more frequently if events or changes in business circumstances indicate the asset might be impaired. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company determined that it had a single, entity</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;wide reporting unit. </font><font style="display: inline;">Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level using a two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;step approach. The first step is to compare the fair value of the reporting unit to the carrying value of the net assets assigned to the reporting unit. If the fair value of the reporting unit is greater than the carrying value of the net assets assigned to the reporting unit, the assigned goodwill is not considered impaired. If the fair value is less than the reporting unit&#x2019;s carrying value, step two is performed to measure the amount of the impairment, if any. In the second step, the fair value of goodwill is determined by deducting the fair value of the reporting unit&#x2019;s identifiable assets and liabilities from the fair value of the reporting unit as a whole, as if the reporting unit had just been acquired and the fair value was being initially allocated. If the carrying value of goodwill exceeds the implied fair value, an impairment charge would be recorded in the period the determination is made.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">At September 30, 2014, the Company determined sufficient indication existed to require performance of an interim goodwill impairment analysis as of September 30, 2014 for the Company&#x2019;s reporting unit.&nbsp;&nbsp;This indicator was a decrease in the Company&#x2019;s market capitalization during the third quarter of 2014&nbsp;below the carrying value of its net assets.&nbsp; Accordingly, in this interim goodwill impairment test, the reporting unit failed step one of the analysis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.2pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The combination of the determination of fair value of the reporting unit and the identification of unrecognized fair value changes to the carrying values of other assets and liabilities in the second step of the interim goodwill impairment test, resulted in an implied fair value of goodwill below the carrying value of goodwill</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> at September 30, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company recorded its best estimate of the goodwill imp</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">airment loss of $57.1 million.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The Company continues t</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">o evaluate the fair value of its</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> goodwill based on the results of its operations. Depending on its operations, the Company may in the future be required to record additional impairment charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Identifiable Intangible Assets</font>

These assets were recorded at their estimated fair values at the acquisition date and are being amortized over their respective estimated useful lives using the straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line method.</font>

Recoverability of the long</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;lived asset is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of the asset or asset group to future undiscounted net cash flows expected to be generated by the asset or asset group. If such assets are not recoverable, the impairment to be recognized, if any, is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the estimated fair value of the assets or asset group. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">During the three months ended September 30, 2014, the Company determined that its technology and customer relationship assets were not fully recoverable due to lower projected revenue levels from associated products and customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company recognized an impairment charge of </font><font style="display: inline;">$36.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million to reduce the carrying values of these intangible assets to their estimated fair values.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value was estimated using an income-based approach based on management&#x2019;s forecast of future cash flows to be derived from the asset&#x2019;s use.&nbsp;&nbsp;There was </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> impairment recorded during the year</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> ended December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2012</font><font style="display: inline;">, or </font><font style="display: inline;">during the period from October 1</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2014 to December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company continues t</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">o evaluate the fair value of its</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> intangible assets based on the results of its operations. Depending on its operations, the Company may in the future be required to record additional impairment charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method of accounting. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases, as well as for operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in the results of operations in the period that includes the enactment date. The measurement of a deferred tax asset is reduced, if necessary, by a valuation allowance if it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. Any excess tax benefit above amounts previously recorded for stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation expense is recorded in additional paid</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;in</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;capital in the consolidated balance sheets to the extent that cash taxes payable are reduced. The Company uses the with</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;and</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;without approach when determining when excess tax benefits have been realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for uncertain tax positions by recognizing the financial statement effects of a tax position only when, based on the technical merits of the position, it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has a policy to recognize interest and penalties accrued on any uncertain tax positions as a component of income tax expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Advertising Costs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company expenses advertising costs as incurred. Advertising costs totaled </font><font style="display: inline;">$124,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$168,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, and </font><font style="display: inline;">$76,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the year</font><font style="display: inline;">s ended December 31, 2014, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2012, respectively. Advertising costs are included within sales and marketing expenses on the consolidated statements of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Technology and Development</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Technology and development expense primarily consists of salaries and payroll</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;related costs for employees, including stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation and bonuses. Additional expenses include costs related to the development, quality assurance and testing of new technology and enhancement of existing technology, amortization of internally developed software related to the Company&#x2019;s technology infrastructure, consulting, travel and other related overhead.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Technology and development costs are expensed as incurred, except for certain costs relating to internally developed software, which are capitalized and amortized on a straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line basis over </font><font style="display: inline;">their estimated useful life</font><font style="display: inline;"> once the asset is placed in service.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Foreign Operations and Currency</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements include the results of the Company&#x2019;s wholly owned subsidiaries whose books and records are maintained in a functional currency other than the U.S. Dollar. Foreign currency transaction losses totaled </font><font style="display: inline;">$44,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$194,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$7,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the years ended December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2014, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2012, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;">, and are included</font><font style="display: inline;"> in general and administrative expenses in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated statement of operations</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stock</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#8209;Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based payment awards for employees by measuring services received in exchange for all equity awards granted based on the fair value of the award as of the grant date. The Company recognizes stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation expense on a straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line basis over the awards&#x2019; vesting period, adjusted for estimated forfeitures. The Company accounts for stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based payment awards for non</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;employees by measuring services received in exchange for all equity awards granted based on the fair value of the award as of the grant date. Fair value is remeasured each reporting period. The Company recognizes non</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;employee stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation expense on a straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line basis over the awards&#x2019; vesting period, adjusted for estimated forfeitures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company uses the Black</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;Scholes option pricing model for estimating the fair value of stock options. The use of the option valuation model requires the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the expected lif</font><font style="display: inline;">e</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the expected stock price volatility based on </font><font style="display: inline;">a combination of the Company&#x2019;s historical price data and </font><font style="display: inline;">peer companies, as there is not enough historical price data for the Company&#x2019;s common stock. Additionally, the recognition of expense requires the estimation of the number of options that will ultimately vest and the number of options that will ultimately be forfeited.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Basic and Dilutive Loss per Common Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company uses the two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;class method to compute net loss per common share because the Company has issued securities, other than common stock, that contractually entitle the holders to participate in dividends and earnings of the Company. The two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;class method requires earnings for the period to be allocated between common stock and participating securities based upon their respective rights to receive distributed and undistributed earnings. Holders of each series of the Company&#x2019;s redeemable convertible preferred stock (prior to the conversion to common stock) and the restricted common stock issued in the May 2011 acquisition of Condaptive,&nbsp;Inc. (&#x201C;Condaptive&#x201D;) are entitled to participate in distributions, when and if declared by the board of directors, that are made to common stockholders, and as a result are considered participating securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;class method, for periods with net income, basic net income per common share is computed by dividing the net income attributable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period. Net income attributable to common stockholders is computed by subtracting from net income the portion of current year earnings that the participating securities would have been entitled to receive pursuant to their dividend rights had all of the year&#x2019;s earnings been distributed. No such adjustment to earnings is made during periods with a net loss, as the holders of the participating securities have no obligation to fund losses. Diluted net loss per common share is computed under the two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;class method by using the weighted</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;average number of shares of common stock outstanding, plus, for periods with net income attributable to common stockholders, the potential dilutive effects of stock options and warrants. In addition, the Company analyzes the potential dilutive effect of the outstanding participating securities under the &#x201C;if</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;converted&#x201D; method when calculating diluted earnings per share, in which it is assumed that the outstanding participating securities convert into common stock at the beginning of the period. The Company reports the more dilutive of the approaches (two class or &#x201C;if</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;converted&#x201D;) as its diluted net income per share during the period. Due to net losses for the year</font><font style="display: inline;">s ended December 31, 2014, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2012, basic and diluted loss per share were the same, as the effect of potentially dilutive securities would have been antidilutive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognized $7.9&nbsp;million of acquisition</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;related costs related t</font><font style="display: inline;">o the acquisition of Jumptap during the year ended December 31,</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">which amount is</font><font style="display: inline;"> included in general and administrative expenses on the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Metaresolver</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On April&nbsp;1, 2013, the Company completed the acquisition of all of the outstanding stock of Metaresolver,&nbsp;Inc. (&#x201C;Metaresolver&#x201D;), a technology and data company focused on analyzing volumes of data from real</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;time bidding exchanges to help brands and agencies optimize their buy and deliver more relevant promotions. The cash consideration for the acquisition of Metaresolver was $13.7&nbsp;million, of which $</font><font style="display: inline;">2.0 million represented</font><font style="display: inline;"> potential deferred cash payments to certain of the Metaresolver founders. The deferred cash payments were subject to varying service requirements over a two</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;year period following the closing of the acquisition, were contingent on the Metaresolver founders&#x2019; continued service with the Company and was recognized as compensation expense on a straight</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;line basis over the requisite service period. For tax purposes, the $2.0&nbsp;million was included in the purchase price. Only $1.0 million of deferred cash payments were earned and paid out as of December 31, 2014. No further payments of the deferred cash are required.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Metaresolver acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting. The consolidated financial statements of the Company for the year ended December 31, 2013 include the financial position and results of operations of Metaresolver from the acquisition date of April&nbsp;1, 2013.</font>
		</p>

Reserves are established in connection with such matters when a loss is probable and the amount of such loss can be reasonably estimated. The determination of probability and the estimation of the actual amount of any such loss are inherently unpredictable, and it is therefore possible that the eventual outcome of such claims and litigation could exceed the estimated reserves. Based upon the Company&#x2019;s experience, current information and applicable law, it does not believe it is reasonably possible that any proceedings and claims will have a material effect on its financial statements. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Line of Credit</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In August 2011, the Company entered into a line of credit with Silicon Valley Bank, or SVB, which allowed for borrowings up to $15.0&nbsp;million. Amounts borrowed under the line of credit are secured by substantially all of the Company&#x2019;s assets. The loan agreement was amended in October 2013 to extend the maturity date to May 9, 2014, to revise the interest rate payable under the agreement and to make other changes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan agreement was amended again in May 2014 increasing allowed borrowings to $20.0 million. The loan agreement was amended and restated in November 2014, increasing allowed borrowings to $40.0 million and making other changes. Advances under the line of credit bear interest at a floating rate equal to, at the Company&#x2019;s option, either the prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal plus a margin of 1.6% or the ICE Benchmark Administration LIBOR rate plus a margin of 2.6%, in either case with interest payable monthly. The line of credit agreement requires that the Company maintain a ratio of cash, cash equivalents and billed </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with the acquisition of Condaptive on May&nbsp;6, 2011, the Company issued 1,448,080 shares of restricted common stock to the employee shareholders of Condaptive. Under the terms of the stock restriction agreements, a portion of the shares of common stock issued was released from restriction on May&nbsp;6, 2012, the first anniversary of the issuance. Thereafter, shares of common stock will be released from restriction on a monthly basis over a period that expires between May 2014 and January 2015, depending on the individual award, so long as the shareholder remains an employee of the Company as of the date of each such release, until all of the common stock is released from restriction. If the shareholder&#x2019;s employment terminates prior to the release of all shares from restriction, the shares not yet vested are subject to repurchase by the Company at a price of $0.001 per share. As of December 31, 2014, 1,448,053 of the shares had been released from restriction.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred income taxes reflect the net tax effect of temporary differences that exist between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and the amounts used for income tax purposes, using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse. As of December 31, 2014, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">$260.9</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million of federal net operating loss carryforwards, which expire at various dates through 2034. The gross amount of the state net operating loss carryforwards is equal to or less than the federal net operating loss carryforwards and expires over various periods based on individual state tax law. As of December 31, 2014, the Company had gross foreign net operating loss carryforwards of </font><font style="display: inline;">$55,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> that do not expire. In addition, the Company </font><font style="display: inline;">had</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$5.3</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million </font><font style="display: inline;">of R&amp;D credits </font><font style="display: inline;">which expire at various dates through 2034</font><font style="display: inline;">, of which $1.2 million were acquired from the Nexage acqu</font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">sition</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2014, the Company had $35.9&nbsp;million in excess tax benefits related to stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;based compensation deductions, the benefit of which will be recorded to additional paid</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;in</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;capital once the benefit is realized through a reduction of income taxes payable. The Company uses the with</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;and</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;without approach when determining when excess tax benefits have been realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In general, businesses with U.S. net operating losses (&#x201C;NOLs&#x201D;) are considered loss corporations for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Pursuant to Section&nbsp;382 of the Code, loss corporations that undergo an ownership change, as defined under the Code, may be subject to an annual limitation on the amount of NOLs (and certain other tax attributes) available to offset taxable income earned after such ownership change. The Company has performed an analysis of its ownership changes pursuant to the rules prescribed under U.S. tax law and preliminarily determined that it experienced two ownership changes since its inception. Based on this analysis, the Company&#x2019;s NOLs and other tax attributes are limited under Section&nbsp;382 of the Code, although the Company does not believe that such limitations will prevent the Company from utilizing its NOLs and other tax attributes in the future. Instead, the realizability of the Company&#x2019;s U.S. NOLs and other tax attributes are dependent on the Company earning sufficient taxable income to utilize its NOLs prior to their respective expiration.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise about which separate financial information is available that is evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker, in deciding how to allocate resources and assess performance. The Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s chief operating decision maker is its Chief Executive Officer (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">CEO</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">). The CEO reviews financial information presented on a consolidated basis for purposes of allocating resources and evaluating financial performance. As such, the Company has concluded that its operations constitute one operating and reportable segment.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;9A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Controls and Procedures</font><a name="Item9AControlsandProcedures_156226"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the supervision of and with the participation of our management, including our chief executive officer, who is our principal executive officer, and our chief financial officer, who is our principal financial officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, the end of the period covered by this Annual Report. The term </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">disclosure controls and procedures,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> as set forth in Rules&nbsp;13a</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;">15(e) and 15d</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or the Exchange Act, means controls and other procedures of a company that are designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by a company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported, within the time periods specified in the SEC</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by a company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to the company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s management, including its principal executive and principal financial officers, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving their objectives, and management necessarily applies its judgment in evaluating the cost</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;benefit relationship of possible controls and procedures. Based on the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, our chief executive officer and chief financial officer concluded that, as of such date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We completed the acquisition of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Inc. (&#x201C;Nexage&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;">on </font><font style="display: inline;">December 4</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">. Management considers this transaction to be material to our consolidated financial statements and believes that the internal controls and procedures of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;"> have a material effect on our internal control over financial reporting. We are currently in the process of incorporating the internal controls and procedures of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;"> into our internal controls over financial reporting and extending our compliance program to include </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;">. We have excluded </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;"> from the scope of our 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> assessment of internal control over financial reporting as provided by applicable law and SEC rules and regulations concerning business combinations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Other than the Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;"> acquisition noted above, there have been no changes in our internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;">15(f)) identified in connection with the evaluation required by Rule&nbsp;13a</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;</font><font style="display: inline;">15(d) of the Exchange Act that occurred during the quarter ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Management</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and Attestation Report of Registered Public Accounting Firm</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> based on the criteria set forth </font><font style="display: inline;">in</font><font style="display: inline;"> the 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Internal Control</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Based on our assessment, management has concluded that, as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, our internal control over financial reporting was effective based on those criteria.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management has excluded the operations of </font><font style="display: inline;">Nexage</font><font style="display: inline;"> from its assessment of internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">. Thes</font><font style="display: inline;">e assets acquired represent</font><font style="display: inline;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;"> $20.8&nbsp;million and $1.5</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million of total and net assets, respectively as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $1.4</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million of total revenues for the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
